vulnerability_analysis: The destroyBlackFunds() function in the BlackList contract subtracts dirtyFunds from _totalSupply without using SafeMath and without checking that dirtyFunds <= _totalSupply. This allows an underflow when destroying more funds than the total supply, making _totalSupply wrap around to a very large number. After the underflow, the owner can issue new tokens up to the amount that doesn't cause an overflow in the issue() function's require check.
attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner. 2. Issue tokens to a new address. 3. Redeem most tokens to reduce total supply below the target address balance. 4. Blacklist the target address. 5. Call destroyBlackFunds() to trigger underflow. 6. Issue new tokens (up to the safe amount). 7. Transfer tokens to attacker.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.startPrank() to impersonate the owner. 2. Create a helper address. 3. Call issue() to mint tokens to owner, then transfer to helper. 4. Call redeem() to reduce total supply below helper's balance. 5. Call addBlackList() on helper. 6. Call destroyBlackFunds() on helper to trigger underflow. 7. Calculate safe amount to issue (type(uint256).max - _totalSupply - 1). 8. Call issue() with safe amount. 9. Transfer newly minted tokens to attacker.
